title: Cooperative GPU Drain & Interruptibility Playbook
author: Priya Nair
body:
Summary:

This playbook defines the cooperative GPU draining and interruptibility model for Redwood’s inference fleet, the configuration primitives and runtime behaviors required from model-serving components, and the operational runbook for planned and emergency node drains. The guidance balances availability, unit cost, and tenant fairness while enabling resumable and preemptible inference where appropriate.

Goals:
- Minimize user-visible failures during node transitions (planned maintenance, autoscaler evictions, capacity rebalancing).
- Ensure fair share across tenants under transient resource pressure.
- Provide clear, auditable procedures for safe drains and emergency recovery.
- Define observable signals and thresholds to trigger automated mitigations.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all GPU-backed inference pools managed by Redwood (hosted + dedicated).
- Covers kernel-level preemption behavior, serving runtime contracts, edge proxy routing, and autoscaler interactions.
- Does not replace dedicated on-prem customer runbooks but provides a reference to adapt to private deployment constraints.

Key terminology:
- Interruptibility Level: Enum applied to a model or route describing how the request can be handled during preemption. Values: non_interruptible, resumable, best_effort, stateless.
- Cooperative Drain: A drain process where the orchestration layer negotiates with the serving runtime and proxies to shift traffic before GPU eviction.
- Locality Routing: Preferential routing to keep a session on the same node/shard to retain KV cache affinity; degrades as nodes are drained.
- Eviction Window: Configurable timeframe during which a drained host accepts only low-priority or resumable work.

Policy: Interruptibility and routing
- Default assignment: All production chat/text-generation routes default to resumable. Short-running sync-only endpoints may be stateless. Latency- critical structured-output endpoints may be marked non_interruptible after product review.
- Model owners must declare interruptibility in the model manifest (model_manifest.interruptibility = "resumable" | "stateless" | "non_interruptible" | "best_effort").
- During cooperative drains, requests that map to resumable models must expose sufficient checkpointing/continuation tokens (KV cache checkpoints or generation cursor) to allow client-side or proxy resume. The serving runtime must provide resume metadata in the response envelope.

Runtime contract (requirements placed on eng-serving-runtime):
1) Session checkpoint API: For resumable routes, serving runtime must produce a resume_token (opaque string) at configurable checkpoints (every N tokens or at stanza boundaries).
2) Graceful slowdown mode: Runtime must support a per-connection "drain hint" that allows in-progress requests to be deprioritized and allowed to finish within an eviction soft-limit (default 30s).
3) Cache export/import: Node-local KV cache snapshots for active sessions must be serializable and transferable to another node within 45s.
4) Hot-path routing hook: Expose metadata to the edge (X-Instance-Locality: true/false) for routing decisions.

Eviction policy primitives (cluster config):
|| key || description || typical default || allowed values ||
|| drain.eviction_soft_limit || time allowed for in-flight resumable requests to finish before forced cancellation || 30s || 10s..120s ||
|| drain.eviction_hard_limit || maximum time before VM/container is forcibly stopped || 90s || 60s..300s ||
|| drain.low_priority_ratio || fraction of capacity reserved for low-priority work during an Eviction Window || 0.10 || 0.0..0.5 ||
|| drain.resume_checkpoint_interval_tokens || tokens between automatic resume checkpoints for long generations || 128 || 16..1024 ||
|| drain.locality_affinity_decay || how quickly affinity is treated as stale during re-routing || 600s || 60s..3600s ||

Behavioral flow (planned maintenance):
1) Initiate: infra initiates drain via redwoodctl: redwoodctl drain-node --node NODE_ID --reason "kernel-upgrade" --window 10m
2) Preflight checks (automated):
   a) Evaluate pool utilization and estimate disruption score.
   b) Check outstanding canary rollouts or model-rating changes. Abort if critical rollouts are in progress.
3) Cooperative negotiation (automated):
   a) Orchestrator marks node as DRAINING and sets drain.eviction_soft_limit timers.
   b) Edge proxies stop sending new non-resumable, non-statsful requests (routing folded to other replicas).
   c) Runtime receives drain hint and starts emitting resume_tokens for new resumable requests and accelerates checkpoint intervals.
4) Traffic shift: Requests are gradually shifted over a 5-15 minute window weighted by session locality and tenant priority.
5) Finalization: After eviction_hard_limit expires or all live sessions finished, the node is cordoned and removed from service.

Behavioral flow (autoscaler/forced preemption):
- If autoscaler signals immediate preemption (e.g., capacity reclaim), system must attempt a fast cooperative drain with reduced soft_limit (default 10s) and raise low_priority_ratio to at least 0.25 to accept only low-cost resumable jobs. If the runtime cannot honor the shorter soft_limit, the autoscaler should prefer different eviction targets (see heuristics below).

Routing heuristics for fairness and locality:
- Prefer to evict nodes with lowest active resumable session count and highest proportion of best_effort / low_priority work.
- When multiple equivalent nodes exist, choose the one with the lowest tenant priority-weighted revenue impact metric.
- Avoid evicting nodes hosting >X non_interruptible sessions (configurable; default X=2) where possible.

Observability and SLOs (what to monitor):
- drain.session_resume_rate (ratio of successful resumes after draining) Target: >= 99.5% over 24h.
- drain.forced_cancellations_per_shift (count per 1000 sessions) Target: <= 0.5
- pooling.eviction_retries (times node had to be reattempted for drain due to runtime non-response) Target: 0 per week
- latency.p95_in_flight_during_drain (milliseconds) Alert if p95 increases > 2x baseline for >10m
- metric tags: model_id, node_id, tenant_id, interruptibility_level, region

Alerting thresholds (suggested):
- SEV-1: drain.session_resume_rate < 97% for 30m or forced_cancellations_per_shift spikes > 5 per 1000 -> paging to infra-sre + eng-serving-runtime
- SEV-2: eviction_retries > 3 in 1h -> on-call infra
- SEV-3: p95 latency delta > 2x for >1h -> product and platform channels

Operational runbook (step-by-step):
Planned drain follow-up (owner: infra-sre)
1) Run preflight: redwoodctl drain-check NODE_ID -> confirm estimated disruption < threshold.
2) Start cooperative drain: redwoodctl drain-node --node NODE_ID --soft 30s --hard 90s --notify "maintenance-schedule-2026-02"
3) Monitor metrics dashboard: drain.session_resume_rate, latency.p95_in_flight_during_drain, edge.request_rejections.
4) If resume_rate falls < 99%:
   a) Pause additional drains in region.
   b) Request serving-runtime to increase checkpoint frequency: POST /internal/runtime/manage -d '{"node": "NODE_ID", "checkpoint_interval_tokens": 64}'
   c) Notify product owners of impacted models for potential mitigation (increase replicas).
5) After node cordon, verify no stale references in routing tables and run redwoodctl cleanup-node NODE_ID.

Emergency forced preemption (owner: oncall infra-sre)
1) If a node is being reclaimed immediately and cooperative drain fails: mark node as EMERGENCY and set low_priority_ratio=1.0 to prevent new non-resumable work.
2) Invoke fallback routing policy: edge-reroute --from NODE_ID --policy immediate --drain-window 10s
3) If forced cancellations exceed safe threshold, open an incident and involve eng-serving-runtime to examine resume_token generation and cache snapshot latency.

Rollout and verification checklist (engineering release lead):
- Confirm model manifests for in-scope models include interruptibility and resume semantic docs.
- Deploy runtime agent change in canary (5% nodes) and verify resume_token appears in responses for resumable routes.
- Run synthetic drain test: simulate drain on canary node and validate session_resume_rate >= 99.5% and forced cancellations < 0.2%.
- Gradually expand to 25%, 50%, then 100% with 24h observation windows.

Testing guidance and synthetic tests:
- Synthetic long-run generator: create 10k resumable sessions per region generating 5k tokens across 2h; trigger drain and verify checkpoint export/import completes within 45s on average.
- Regression test: ensure non_interruptible routes are never involuntarily moved during a short-window autoscaler reclaim (assertion in CI).

Implementation notes and examples:
- Example model manifest snippet (YAML):
  model_id: gptx-4-mini
  interruptibility: resumable
  resume_semantics: "opaque resume_token present on partial_response.headers.X-Resume-Token"
  checkpointing: 
    interval_tokens: 128
    export_endpoint: https://internal-cache-export.redwood/services

- Example cluster override (yaml):
  drain:
    eviction_soft_limit: "30s"
    eviction_hard_limit: "90s"
    low_priority_ratio: 0.10
    locality_affinity_decay: "600s"

- CLI examples:
  - redwoodctl drain-node --node i-gpu-029 --soft 30s --hard 90s --reason "kpatch"
  - redwoodctl drain-check --node i-gpu-029

Heuristics for autoscaler (decision guidance):
- Prefer nodes with high stateless workload fraction > 60% when selecting preemption targets.
- If all nodes have high non_interruptible counts, prefer region-level capacity shifts rather than single-node preempts.

Ownership and escalation:
- Primary owner: infra-sre (oncall: infra-sre@redwood.internal)
- Secondary owner: eng-serving-runtime (runtime-oncall@redwood.internal)
- Reviewer cadence: bi-annual review of metrics and thresholds (owners must update this doc after each review).

Related artifacts and links:
- Runtime API spec for checkpointing (internal link: eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture/checkpointing-api)
- Autoscaler eviction heuristics (internal link: eng-infra/gpu-fleet-and-capacity/autoscaler-eviction-heuristics-2025)

Appendix: quick incident template to record drain-related postmortems:
- Incident ID:
- Node ID(s):
- Event timeline (UTC):
- Root cause summary:
- Mitigations applied (temporary):
- Long term actions and owner:

Notes and rationale:
- We intentionally blend cooperative and emergency behaviors to allow graceful human-scheduled maintenance while retaining the ability to reclaim capacity quickly for platform health. The resume_token approach minimizes duplication of cost while giving product teams control over consistency semantics.
